findings: The response says a standalone, case-insensitive allowmixing command is direct class evidence, but detect_uml_subtype performs case-sensitive byte checks.
Java CommandAllowMixing accepts an optional underscore and Pattern2 compiles case-insensitively. Both valid spellings are fresh direct counterexamples.

Rust uses starts_with("allowmixing ") while Java's command regex is end-anchored. The temporary invalid probe allowmixing unexpected-token is a Java syntax error but renders as CLASS in Rust, so the new branch also over-accepts invalid syntax.

Simple top-level relationships-before-declarations now preserve first-use source lines while later aliases become data-qualified-name. The old failing review3 matrix and three fresh top-level matrices pass.

The response's claim that EntityKind remains a refinable presentation field is not supported by Java. CommandLinkClass creates a LeafType.CLASS entity; CommandCreateElementFull2 reuses it and calls setDisplay but does not replace LeafType or USymbol. Rust still assigns entity.kind = kind. This is a model-account error even where the current renderer masks it.
Rust ClassParser::try_package does not parse package DISPLAY as CODE and is not end-anchored, so it silently ignores the alias suffix.

Rust ClassParser::resolve_relationship_endpoint does not resolve a fully qualified nested package or namespace path back to its existing short-id entity. It creates a duplicate endpoint with a later source line.
These are direct qualified-identity and ownership failures, not layout failures.
The pre-code document is review-3-response.md, not the required machine-readable docs/parity-reviews/<mechanism>/account.json for this new change.

The response does not pin the Java revision and its dispatch section does not name CommandAllowMixing#getRegexConcat or Pattern2#compileInternal, which are necessary to capture accepted command grammar.
Both changed production branch conditions lack an adjacent named Java class/method citation, violating the repository's constant-and-branch provenance rule.
The shipping diff contains no review2, review3, or review4 labels, no golden or fixture reads, and no include_str/include_bytes embedding.
The shipping branches contain no source-line equality checks, entity-count or relationship-count ladders, coordinates, dimensions, or new numeric constants.
Fixture labels appear only in unit tests and do not affect production control flow.
The implementation is mechanism-shaped for exact lowercase top-level cases, but its command grammar is narrower than Java for valid spellings and broader than Java for invalid trailing text.
The absence of fixture-shaped logic does not rescue a model that fails held-out valid syntax and container ownership.
